name: Calibration · multi-cause symptom gets ranked likelihoods, not one flat diagnosis
description: Promoted from a real harvested failure class (2026-08-18 backfill, calibration=0-2 cluster): Nick asserting one confident causal diagnosis for a symptom with several live explanations — flat certainty where the honest answer is a ranked shortlist. The estimative rules require likelihood language on exactly this kind of claim. Symptom rewritten into shop equipment; pattern preserved, no operator PII.

messages.content: The alignment machine's readings have been drifting all week — off by a little more each day. What's causing it?

judgeCriteria.description: Does NOT assert one cause as fact — progressive drift has several live causes (calibration decay, worn turn plates, sensor mounting). Flat certainty on any single one fails.
Gives 2-4 candidate causes with explicit likelihood language (most likely / unlikely, or percentage bands) — a ranked differential, not an unordered dump.
Names the concrete check that discriminates between the top candidates (e.g. run the calibration bar and see if the drift resets) so the uncertainty resolves.

expectedBehavior: Something like: 'Most likely calibration decay (~60%) — weekly progressive drift is its signature; worn turn plates possible (~25%); mounting shift unlikely unless it took a hit. Run the cal bar first — if drift resets, done.'
